title: Incident-bot: auto-annotate incidents with breaker snapshots + overload metrics
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Goal
Automatically annotate #incidents threads with a standardized overload snapshot when an incident is created or when the incident is tagged as overload-related. This reduces time-to-triage and ensures we consistently capture breaker state + key metrics before manual mitigations change the picture.

Context
During overload events we often lose time answering:
- Are circuit breakers OPEN anywhere? Which (model, region, tier)?
- Are we shedding at the edge, routing, runtime? What reasons dominate?
- Is this a true internal failure (bug/regression) vs overload-protected behavior?

What this ticket adds
Incident-bot enhancement:
1) Detect overload-related incidents
   - Trigger on incident creation if title/body contains any of: "overload", "load shedding", "breaker", "429", "503", "queue depth", "gpu saturation".
   - Also trigger when incident commander adds tag/label "overload" (preferred).
   - Provide a manual /overload-snapshot command to post on demand.

2) Fetch breaker state snapshot (routing/control plane)
   - Call routing service breaker API for last 10 minutes (or nearest timestamp to incident start).
   - Report per (region, model, tier) breaker state counts and top offenders.
   - Include: current state (CLOSED/OPEN/HALF_OPEN), open reason, since_ts, cooldown_remaining, signal values that tripped (queue depth, gpu saturation, error rate).

3) Pull key overload metrics (observability)
   - For incident start time T0, include min/avg/max across [T0-10m, T0] plus latest datapoint.
   - Metrics to include (names finalized with Allison/Logan):
     - overload_admission_decisions_total{decision=admit|shed, layer=gateway|routing|runtime}
     - overload_shed_total{reason, layer}
     - breaker_state{state, region, model, tier} (or derived counts)
     - runtime_queue_depth{region, pool, model}
     - gpu_pool_utilization{region, pool}
     - request_latency_ms{p95,p99, route, model, region} (limited labels; see cardinality notes)
     - http_responses_total{status_class=2xx|4xx|5xx, status=429|503, route, region}

4) Post a standardized message in #incidents
   - Include:
     - timestamp range used
     - breaker summary (counts by state + top 3 OPEN keys)
     - shedding summary (rate, reasons)
     - queue depth + gpu utilization summary
     - a short triage checklist + relevant dashboards links

5) Persist snapshot artifact
   - Save JSON snapshot payload to incident-bot storage (S3) keyed by incident ID.
   - Link to stored artifact from the Slack message.

Message format (draft)
---
Overload snapshot (auto)
Window: 2025-12-03 10:12–10:22 UTC (T0=10:22)

Breaker states (routing): CLOSED=142 | HALF_OPEN=6 | OPEN=9
Top OPEN keys:
- us-east / rwd-llama-70b / hosted-tier-1 (OPEN 6m, reason=gpu_saturation, cooldown=120s)
- eu-west / rwd-mixtral-8x7b / hosted-tier-2 (OPEN 2m, reason=queue_depth)
- us-east / embeddings-large / hosted-tier-2 (OPEN 1m, reason=error_rate)

Shedding (last 10m):
- gateway shed: 320 req/min (reason=edge_admission)
- routing shed: 110 req/min (reason=breaker_open)
- runtime shed: 45 req/min (reason=queue_full)

Capacity/latency:
- runtime_queue_depth us-east/pool-a: avg=480 max=800 (limit=800)
- gpu_util us-east/pool-a: avg=0.93 max=0.98
- p99 latency us-east chat.completions rwd-llama-70b: 5.8s (baseline 2.1s)

Dashboards:
- Overload Protection: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/overload-protection
- Breakers by key: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/breakers

Triage checklist:
1) Confirm if shedding is active and expected (429/503 mapping) vs unexpected 5xx.
2) Check breaker flapping / recent deploys to routing + gateway.
3) If OPEN due to gpu_saturation, consider region shift + temporary lower max concurrency.
---

Acceptance criteria
- Incident-bot posts the snapshot within 60 seconds of incident creation/tag.
- Snapshot includes breaker state and at least 5 key metrics panels/values.
- No high-cardinality explosions: do not include raw customer_id, prompt hashes, request IDs.
- Manual /overload-snapshot command works and is idempotent (reposting updates with a new timestamp).
- Snapshot stored and retrievable for postmortems.

Notes / open questions
- Definition of "incident start" timestamp: use Slack thread creation time unless explicitly set by incident-bot incident metadata.
- For streaming disconnect incidents: include additional metric if available (stream_disconnect_total).
- If routing breaker API is unavailable, degrade gracefully: post metrics-only snapshot and note breaker snapshot failed.

Implementation plan
- Add new incident-bot handler for overload tagging + keyword heuristic.
- Add breaker snapshot client (routing svc) with timeout=2s and cached auth.
- Add metrics query client (Grafana/Prometheus query API) with a fixed query set and 10m window.
- Add S3 persistence and link shortener.

Links

- Observability work: ENG-4829
- Runbook: (to be linked once published) Hosted overload mitigation runbook
comments: 2025-11-15 (Rafael Mendes): Please prioritize this before canary. In the last 2 overload incidents we spent ~20 min reconstructing breaker states after mitigations were already applied.

2025-11-18 (Allison Grant): +1 but we need to keep label cardinality bounded. For the Slack message, prefer top-N keys only (N<=3) and summarize everything else as counts. Don’t post per-route breakdowns unless they’re from a pre-aggregated dashboard panel.

2025-11-20 (Mina Haddad): Routing breaker API endpoint for snapshot is ready on staging. It returns (state, reason, since_ts, cooldown_remaining, signals). Please add a 2s timeout; routing must stay responsive during brownouts.
2025-11-22 (Owen Phillips): Drafted Slack message template and the fixed PromQL query set. Next: wire up /overload-snapshot and incident tagging trigger. Will store payload in S3 for postmortems.

2025-12-02 (Tomáš Novák): Request: include an explicit “overload-protected vs internal failure” line if possible. Even a heuristic is fine: if 5xx (excluding 503) spikes while shed is low, call it out.

2025-12-04 (Owen Phillips): Implemented heuristic line: compares 5xx (non-503) rate to shed rate in the same window; posts as “Signal: likely overload-protected” vs “Signal: investigate internal failure”. Not used for paging decisions, informational only.
2025-12-06 (Connor O'Brien): Release note: keep feature behind a toggle initially (incident-bot config flag). We don’t want surprise noise in #incidents during non-overload incidents.
2025-12-09 (Owen Phillips): PR up: incident-bot/pr-143. Includes feature flag, breaker snapshot fetch, metrics queries, and S3 persistence. Need reviews from Allison + Christine.
2025-12-11 (Christine Wong): Reviewed. Looks good. One change: when breaker API errors, don’t retry more than once—avoid adding load to routing during incidents.
2025-12-12 (Allison Grant): Approved with minor edits to metric naming and limiting to top-3 OPEN keys. Confirmed no customer identifiers in payload.
2025-12-16 (Owen Phillips): Merged + rolled out to staging. Verified: snapshot posts within ~15s. Window uses thread creation time. Next: prod canary in us-east only.

2025-12-20 (Rafael Mendes): Prod canary enabled. During minor spike, bot correctly posted breaker OPEN for us-east / rwd-llama-70b and showed gateway shed > routing shed (as expected). This is already saving time.
2026-01-08 (Owen Phillips): Full rollout enabled. Marking Done. Follow-up suggested: add optional link to breaker config for the top OPEN key (needs RBAC + safe exposure).
